title: From Arc to Dia: Lessons learned building AI Browsers – Samir Mody, The Browser Company of New York
talk_summary: Samir Mody describes The Browser Company's shift from Arc to the AI-native Dia browser, emphasizing fast iteration tooling, prompt optimization via the GEPA reflective-mutation method, treating model behavior as a discipline, and designing product UX around prompt-injection risk. Most content is product/org philosophy, but a few mechanisms (GEPA-style prompt hill-climbing, in-product prompt tooling, human confirmation gates) are copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Seed a set of prompt variants, run them across a task set, score outputs, select the best via Pareto selection, then use an LLM to reflect on what worked and mutate new prompts, iterating without RL or fine-tuning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: seed the system with a set of prompts, then execute it across a set of tasks and score them... leverage an LLM on top of that to reflect on what went well and what didn't and then generate new prompts

takeaways.technique: Prompt/model tooling built into the product everyone uses
takeaways.what_they_do: Moved prompt editing from dev-only builds into the internal product so prompts, tools, context, models, and parameters are editable by anyone with their real personal context, widening who can iterate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we built all of our tools into our product, the product that we as a company internally use every day. And that includes the prompts, the tools, the context, the models, every parameter

takeaways.technique: Human confirmation gate before irreversible external actions
takeaways.what_they_do: For prompt-injection-prone actions (autofill, scheduling, email), show the exact plain-text payload to the user for confirmation before executing, accepting that it doesn't prevent injection but preserves control and trust.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before the form is written to, we actually let the user read and confirm that data in plain text. This doesn't prevent a prompt injection, but it gives the user control

takeaways.what_they_do: After prototyping, they collect and refine evals to clarify product requirements, then hill-climb through code and prompting, then dogfood internally before shipping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we collect and refine eval to clarify product requirements and then hill climb through code through prompting and automated techniques

takeaways.technique: Widen the funnel of who can create agent behaviors
takeaways.what_they_do: Lowered the threshold so non-engineers (PMs, designers, ops) can prototype AI features with their own context, and a strategy/ops person rewrote all prompts over a weekend, unlocking a quality jump.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a person on our team on the strategy and ops team and he actually leveraged these prompt tools one weekend to rewrite all our prompts
